errors: Sum of the 24 squared residuals: the listed constants give exactly 35.630170, not 34.630170 (slip of 1 in the units digit; the decimals agree). With divisor 14 the correct values are 35.630170/14 = 2.545012 and √ = 1.5953 (not 2.473584 and 1.57276).

Divisor '24−10 = 14' is correct only if two stations (Falkenberg, Wilsede) are fixed, leaving 10 unknowns. If all 12 corrections a…m were free (one datum defect would remain for a free network), the redundancy would be 24−11 = 13. The page has faint over-writings ('11', '2') near this number.
Falkenberg's correction a occurs in only one equation (1.3), so that observation has zero redundancy. The non-zero a-row (+0.595) shows it is not adjusted; this is consistent with a being held fixed.
Hamburg −26.564 does not equal Litberg −90.345 + 64.170 = −26.175; Hamburg's value apparently comes from elsewhere. Unresolved.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working application of Gauss's own, well-documented least-squares and mean-error methods to his Hannover survey data. The only items of note are an arithmetic slip in the sum of squares and the fixed-station degrees-of-freedom count.
